text:
The man prevails. The right-of-way was an easement appurtenant that was extinguished by merger when the woman conveyed the house to him, placing the dominant and servient estates in one owner, and an extinguished easement does not revive on a later sale. The warranty deed did not grant a new easement, and no easement by necessity or implication arose: the path was only a more direct route, and the man never possessed or used the house.  
CONFIDENCE: 82
